categories.implied-object: A tool or everyday object is used or missed but never named; the scene's theme words (near_wrong) are different words from the object.
categories.implied-person-role: A profession or role is implied only by what the person does or says; the role word never appears.
categories.implied-place: A common-noun place (not a proper name) is implied by what happens there; scene words that a topic reader would print are in near_wrong.
categories.bridge-entity: Two-step factual statement ending in a complete clause; the concept is the unnamed intermediate entity, not the stated fact.
categories.referent: An entity is introduced under a description, never named, then referred to by a pronoun or possessive; the concept is its name.
categories.implied-material-or-substance: What something is made of, or what is being poured, drawn or collected, is implied by process details and never named.
categories.implied-event: A one-word event is implied through side details; the obvious scene words (near_wrong) are different words.
categories.distractor-theme: A strong surface theme (near_wrong) that is NOT the concept; the concept is one specific unnamed thing inside the scene.
categories.negation-or-contrast: The concept is the thing that is absent, missing or opposite to what everyone else has; never named.
categories.second-language: Unnamed objects described in Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese or Russian; accepted in English, and in the source language where that word is in the single-token list.
categories.control: Plain text with no particular hidden concept; shows what a lens prints when there is nothing to find.
